## Design

### 2026-10-05 — So I’ve never made any hardware before, and I’m new to PCBs. So I started by working out what software to use. I went for EasyEDA and will try KiCad tomorrow. I followed a couple of tutorials to pract

**1.8h**

So I’ve never made any hardware before, and I’m new to PCBs. So I started by working out what software to use. I went for EasyEDA and will try KiCad tomorrow. I followed a couple of tutorials to practice designing a schematic, then turning it into a PCB design and routing all the traces. All analysis I did suggested that these designs would work if I had them printed so that’s good! The final circuit design that I will need to make (a pimped Alice circuit)  is very complex, so I’ll need some more practice. All I will have to work from is a schematic diagram, and will have to recreate it and route the entire PCB myself.

So all that to come! Excited and enjoying it so far!

Here are images of the schematic, PCB and 3D rendering I designed for a simple PCB that powers an LED using a 5V USB-C input and a simple switch.

### 2026-10-06 — Today I started transferring the PCB from the schematic PDF to EasyEDA. This involves finding each individual component and ensuring it has the right values, at a reasonable price and is in stock. So

**1.42h**

Today I started transferring the PCB from the schematic PDF to EasyEDA. This involves finding each individual component and ensuring it has the right values, at a reasonable price and is in stock. So far, component cost is coming to ~$1 which is good.
Going well and it's a really fun process actually. I'm having fun! I just hope I'm doing it right...
